RUN.about: Cut by the API consumer's journey through a blogging platform — the server boots and mounts routes, then a user authenticates, explores profiles, works with articles, and discovers tags — with the Prisma database as shared infrastructure off the path.

issues.title: No 404 for nonexistent target user
issues.detail: Unlike `getProfile`, `followUser` and `unfollowUser` go straight to `prisma.user.update` without checking the user exists. A nonexistent username causes a Prisma P2025 error instead of a clean `HttpException(404)`.

issues.title: No self-follow prevention
issues.detail: Nothing checks whether the authenticated user's id belongs to the target username. A user can follow their own profile, and Prisma silently inserts a self-referencing row in the join table, which also makes the article feed return their own articles.

issues.title: Adding a comment to a missing article crashes
issues.detail: `addComment` calls `article.findUnique` but does not check if the result is null. When the article does not exist, `article?.id` is undefined and Prisma throws a validation error instead of the service returning a clean 404.

issues.title: Delete ignores the slug URL parameter
issues.detail: `deleteComment` receives only the comment id and user id. The `:slug` in the URL is never checked, so a DELETE to `/articles/wrong-slug/comments/42` will delete comment 42 from any article as long as the user owns it.

children.sub: Populates the database with randomly generated demo users, articles, and comments
children.detail: Generates 12 demo users, 144 articles, and 1,728 comments using `@ngneat/falso` for fake data, calling the real service functions to write.

code.label: Generator functions for user, article, comment

rows.title: Create 12 Users
rows.detail: Calls auth.service.createUser with random name, email, password. Each is flagged demo: true.

rows.title: Create 12 Articles Per User
rows.detail: Calls article.service.createArticle with random title, body, and 4 random word tags. 144 articles total.

rows.title: Comment On Every Article
rows.detail: Every user comments on every article via addComment. 12 users × 144 articles = 1,728 comments.

rows.title: Disconnect
rows.detail: Calls prisma.$disconnect() on the script's own PrismaClient, not the singleton the services used.

rows.label: Passwords
rows.value: Random strings bcrypt-hashed by createUser; the plaintext is never stored or logged, so nobody can log in as a seeded user

issues.title: Singleton client never disconnected
issues.detail: The seed script creates its own PrismaClient at line 14 and disconnects it on exit. But all data writes go through service functions that use the singleton from prisma-client.ts, whose connection pool is never closed. The process may hang after seeding.
